articles.text:
Anita Goswami is a Senior Content Producer at Hindustan Times, where she primarily covers Indian and international news. With four years of industry experience, she has led coverage of Indian General elections, Assembly elections, and national polls in the United States, Canada, Bangladesh, and Nepal. Her reporting covers global wars and major events, including Operation Sindoor, Sheikh Hasina's ouster and the Mahakumbh Mela. She verifies facts and uses clear sources to ensure accurate reporting. As former Chief Copy Editor at Storytailors, she managed teams to produce top-quality content for networks like NDTV, Profit, CNBC-TV18, Upstox and News18. Her work is featured in NDTV, Meaww, and Global Pulse. Throughout her tenure, Anita has collaborated with and been mentored by top industry experts. When not reading, Anita can be found outdoors or at a bakery. Fields of interest: Indian political history, international elections, historical policy analysis, global conflicts, cultural events, Formula 1, art, media ethics and reporting on socio-political change over time.
‘The fight is on’: Opposition targets govt over special Parliament sitting, calls it ‘assault’ on Constitution
The Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha secretariats issued bulletins confirming a four-day sitting from November 30 to December 3.
Opposition parties have criticised the BJP-led NDA government's decision to reconvene Parliament from November 30, accusing it of violating constitutional principles.
On Thursday, the Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha secretariats issued bulletins confirming a four-day sitting from November 30 to December 3, with the Lower House meeting first and the Upper House reconvening on December 2. This came after an earlier request by Union parliamentary affairs minister Kiren Rijiju to Speaker Om Birla and Chairman CP Radhakrishnan to reconvene the Houses.
Reacting to the development, Congress general secretary Jairam Ramesh on Thursday alleged that the government was preparing to reintroduce the Constitution amendment bill, which seeks to increase the strength of the Lok Sabha to 850 seats and facilitate the implementation of women's reservation.
Deep Dive
In a post shared on X, Ramesh said that the central government made the delimitation bills public on April 14, Ambedkar Jayanti, before the legislation failed to pass in Parliament on April 17. “Now on Constitution Day, after 105 days of Operation Lotus, the Modi government announces a special session, hoping that it will get its super-tainted two-thirds majority to pass a Constitution amendment bill,” he said.
“Can there be a greater insult to and assault on the Constitution?” Ramesh asked, adding, “The fight is on.”
Congress MP Shashi Tharoor backed Ramesh's remarks, saying the Opposition's fight was to protect democratic institutions.
"Absolutely. The fight is on -- a fight to save Indian democracy, to protect India's unity and to save our Parliament's integrity," Tharoor wrote on X.
Congress leader P Chidambaram on Friday questioned the need for a fresh women's reservation Bill, saying Parliament had already passed the Constitution (106th Amendment) Act in 2023 and that his party had supported it.
Chidambaram said the 2023 amendment had been passed by both Houses of Parliament on September 20 and 21, and that the Congress had supported its passage while demanding its immediate implementation.
"Why is the BJP government not implementing the Act? What is the need for a new Bill?" he asked.
In another post, Chidambaram said the 2023 amendment linked women's reservation to delimitation following the next Census through Article 334A. He argued that removing the article would allow the quota to be implemented immediately.
He said the Congress and other opposition parties had opposed the inclusion of Article 334A during the passage of the Bill, but the BJP had insisted on retaining it.
"All that the BJP has to do is propose to delete Article 334A. Once Article 334A is deleted, women's reservation can be implemented immediately," Chidambaram wrote on X.
Congress general secretary KC Venugopal also accused the government of attempting to undermine democratic institutions through the proposed legislation.
"They are Vote Chors. They are Seat Chors. There is no doubt that their Delimitation Bill will be nothing more than an exercise in Sansad Chori," he said.
"To orchestrate this murder of the Constitution on Constitution Day shows how badly they want to mock our precious democratic system. We will not allow this to pass. Bring it on," Venugopal added.
The BJP has rejected allegations of vote theft, maintaining that the Opposition was blaming the government and constitutional institutions for its electoral setbacks. There was no immediate reaction from the ruling party to the Opposition's fresh allegations.
Rashtriya Janata Dal (RJD) MP Manoj Kumar Jha also took a swipe at the BJP, suggesting that the ruling party may have secured the numbers required to pass the legislation.
"So, the numbers have been 'cooked' by the BJP, and apparently, they used the finest 'cookware' available!" Jha wrote on X.
BJD vice-president Prasanna Acharya said his party had expected Parliament to be reconvened, as the Monsoon Session had been adjourned without being formally prorogued.
Speaking in Bhubaneswar, Acharya said the government had not yet clarified the purpose of the upcoming sitting, but indicated that the delimitation Bill linked to women's reservation could be brought back.
"As speculated, most likely the government is going to bring the Delimitation Bill tagged with the Women's Reservation Bill again," he told ANI. Acharya added that the BJD hoped the government would address the objections raised by opposition parties. "We hope that the points which were objected to by the Opposition parties will be amicably settled and the government will change its stand," he said.
Congress MP Karti P Chidambaram, meanwhile, hinted at a possible change in the political positions of some non-NDA parties.
"Guess the BJP government has got its ducks in a row!" he wrote, tagging the official social media accounts of the BJP, DMK and NCP-SP.
The Communist Party of India (Marxist) also opposed the proposed exercise. CPI(M) MP John Brittas accused the government of using political manoeuvres to secure a majority for delimitation and warned against linking the exercise to women's reservation.
"Women's empowerment must never become a smokescreen for electoral engineering," Brittas said.
Questioning the timing of the announcement, he alleged that the proposed changes were aimed at manufacturing a parliamentary majority rather than reflecting the people's mandate.
"The essence of the Constitution is respect for the people's mandate. Govts must be formed by that mandate, legislate through it, and never subvert it," he wrote on X.
"What is being done in the name of delimitation-amalgamation, merger, acquisition, and buyout designed to manufacture a majority'is nothing short of an assault on the Constitution," he added.
Brittas further warned that the special sitting could become the "saddest chapter in the history of Indian democracy".
"A majority manufactured through political manipulation is not a mandate. It is a mockery of democracy," he said.
On X, Congress MP Tewari said the request “mocks the institution of Parliament”, while adding that it was time for the Winter Session to convene. The government had not prorogued the Monsoon Session, which concluded on August 13.
“A Special Session is a mechanism for convening during the inter-session period. It can and should not become a substitute for a regular winter session,” Tewari wrote. He added, “Why not just convene a regular winter session and the government can if the government chooses too, it can always regurgitate defeated legislation.”
Congress MP Renuka Chowdhury questioned the short duration of the upcoming sitting, saying the government had given the Rajya Sabha only two days after more than 90 days of uncertainty over Parliament's calendar.
In a post on X, she said she had written to Rajya Sabha Chairman CP Radhakrishnan on November 19 seeking clarity on the parliamentary schedule.
"Is this a substitute for the Winter Session? Parliament is not a clearance counter for the Executive. It exists to hold the Government accountable, not rubber-stamp its agenda," she wrote.
BJD leader Prasanna Acharya said the government had not clarified the agenda for the upcoming parliamentary sitting and expressed hope that it would reconsider its position on the delimitation legislation.
"We hope that the points which were objected to by the Opposition parties will be amicably settled and the government will change its stand," he told ANI.
What BJP says
Amit Shah on Thursday reiterated the government's commitment to providing 33% reservation to women, accusing the Congress of holding up its implementation.
"Women will definitely get 33% reservation; this is our resolve," Shah wrote on X.
"Congress has been blocking this. I want to tell Rahul Gandhi today that it is the resolve of the BJP and Prime Minister Narendra Modi that the women of this country will get 33% reservation," he said.
Why the Opposition is objecting
The proposed delimitation legislation seeks to increase the strength of the Lok Sabha from its current 543 elected seats to a maximum of 850. The government has linked the proposed expansion to the implementation of 33% reservation for women in the Lower House.
Parliament passed the Women's Reservation Bill in September 2023 through the Constitution (106th Amendment) Act, also known as the Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam. The law provides for reserving one-third of seats for women in the Lok Sabha, state legislative assemblies and the Delhi legislative assembly, including seats reserved for women from Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes.
The reservation has not yet come into effect. Under the 2023 Act, its implementation is subject to a Census being conducted after the law's commencement and a subsequent delimitation exercise.
Earlier this year, the government introduced the Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill in the Lok Sabha. It proposed increasing the strength of the Lower House to a maximum of 850 seats and changing the existing framework to enable the implementation of women's reservation before the next Census-based delimitation.
The Bill was put to a vote the next day but failed to secure the required two-thirds majority of members present and voting.
The Opposition INDIA bloc has called for implementing the 33% reservation in the existing 543-member Lok Sabha without waiting for an expansion of seats. Opposition parties have also questioned the proposed delimitation exercise, including the use of the 2011 Census as its population reference and its potential impact on the representation of states.
The Opposition earlier also raised concerns that population-based delimitation could give northern states a larger share of Lok Sabha seats while reducing the southern states' relative representation. States such as Tamil Nadu and Kerala say they should not be disadvantaged for controlling population growth.
The government at the time rejected this concern. Amit Shah said the expansion would increase southern states' seats from 129 (out of 543) to 195 (out of 850), keeping their combined share of the Lok Sabha at around 24%. The Opposition, though, sought clarity on the formula for allocating seats.

20 TMC rebels, 22 DMK MPs and Lok Sabha numbers game: Decoding delimitation maths
The Union Cabinet is likely to approve changes to the Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill and the Delimitation Bill
Seven months after suffering its first defeat on a constitutional amendment, the government is returning to Parliament with its plan to redraw India’s political map. The Union Cabinet is likely to meet on Friday to approve changes to the Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill and the Delimitation Bill. The changes aim to allay southern states’ fears about their share of seats.
The government has asked for the Lok Sabha to reconvene on Monday, and the Rajya Sabha on Wednesday.
What do bills do
Deep Dive
The bills aim to bring in 33% reservation for women in the Lok Sabha and state assemblies before the 2029 Lok Sabha election. To do this, a fresh delimitation will be carried out to expand the Lok Sabha. The amendment seeks to raise the Lok Sabha’s strength from 550 to 850, with up to 815 seats for states and 35 for Union Territories. The Rajya Sabha’s ceiling of 250 stays. The Delimitation Bill would base the exercise on the latest census. In practice, this means using the 2011 census. The Delimitation Commission would be headed by a serving or retired Supreme Court judge, with the Chief Election Commissioner or their nominee and the state election commissioner of the state concerned as members.
Why the South objects, and the flat 50% fix
Southern states have been the strongest objectors. Their populations grew more slowly, so if seats are based purely on population, their weight in Parliament shrinks. The fix under discussion is a “flat 50%” formula, under which every state’s seats would rise by half, and the present proportions would stay the same. In April, this was only a spoken promise from Union home minister Amit Shah, backed by a “guarantee” from Prime Minister Narendra Modi, and was not part of the bill. The government is now considering raising seats by up to 50% in every state while keeping the inter-state proportions based on the 1971 Census, though no final decision has been taken.
Law and Justice Ministry (Legislative Department) officials said the revised draft may also restore the 1971 Census as the basis for dividing seats among states, a reference the April bill removed. Without it, a uniform 50% rise for every state would not be possible, since the bill otherwise ties seats to population. The April version carried no state-wise seat numbers or formula, a gap the Opposition repeatedly flagged. Whether the new draft fixes this will be clear only after the Cabinet meets.
On April 17, the amendment bill got 298 votes in favour and 230 against. It needed 352, two-thirds of the 528 members present and voting, and fell 54 short. It was the first Modi government bill to be defeated, and the government withdrew the two bills.
What has changed since
The picture in the Lok Sabha has shifted since April. In June, 20 of Trinamool Congress (TMC)’s 28 Lok Sabha members broke away and merged with the little-known Nationalist Citizens Party of India, which supports the ruling National Democratic Alliance (NDA). In July, Speaker Om Birla approved the merger of six Shiv Sena (UBT) MPs with the Eknath Shinde-led Shiv Sena, an NDA partner.
The Shiromani Akali Dal, which walked out of the NDA in 2020 over the farm laws, has announced its support for the Delimitation Bill and the women’s reservation law. The NDA now has about 320 members in the Lok Sabha. The House has three vacant seats, which leaves it with 540 members. If every member votes, the bill needs 360 for passage.
The numbers game
On its own, the NDA is about 40 votes short. The Sharad Pawar-led Nationalist Congress Party – Sharadchandra Pawar, or NCP (SP), with eight members, could take it to about 328. NCP (SP) leader Supriya Sule has said her party is open to backing the bill if every state gets a flat 50% increase with no state-wise tweaks, but she wants to see the full bill first.
The Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK), which has 22 members, left the Opposition bloc in May after the Congress tied up with ruling Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam in Tamil Nadu. It is expected to decide only after it has seen the draft and received written assurances on its demands. Even with the DMK, the NDA would reach only about 350, still about 10 short.
The remaining votes would have to come from the 15 other members outside both alliances. Besides the DMK, this group includes the Yuvajana Sramika Rythu Congress Party or YSRCP (four), Aam Aadmi Party or AAP (three), Amritpal Singh’s Akali Dal (Waris Punjab De) with two, and one each from the All India Majlis-e-Ittehadul Muslimeen or AIMIM, Chandrashekhar Azad’s party, the United People’s Party Liberal, the Zoram People’s Movement, Engineer Rashid’s party, and an independent.
The YSRCP has often sided with the government on key bills. AAP and the AIMIM are unlikely to support. Even if the YSRCP and a few smaller members joined in, the NDA would reach only about 355-357.
That is where attendance becomes crucial. The two-thirds rule counts only those present. If just five or six opposition members are absent, a tally of about 357 would be enough. If 30 walk out, only 510 vote, and the target drops to 340, which the NDA, NCP(SP) and DMK together would cross comfortably. A constitutional amendment must also be backed by a majority of the House’s total membership, 272 votes, but the government clears that easily.
The 20 lawmakers
This is why the fate of the 20 members matters so much. Abhishek Banerjee, TMC’s leader in the Lok Sabha, has asked the Speaker to disqualify them under the anti-defection law. The rebels say their move was a valid merger, which the law protects. All 20 sent individual replies to the Speaker on November 24, defending their exit and contesting the petitions. They had sought five extensions since late August to prepare their responses.
The Supreme Court is hearing Banerjee’s plea for a decision within a fixed time. In September, it asked the Speaker to decide “expeditiously” but did not set a deadline.
Under the Tenth Schedule, it is the Speaker, not the Election Commission of India (ECI), who decides such cases, and a member keeps their seat and their vote until a ruling is given. So unless the Speaker decides before Monday, all 20 can vote on the bill. The ECI’s role is a separate one. The rebels have said they will pursue their claim to TMC’s original name and symbol before the TMC.
If the Speaker did disqualify the 20 before the vote, the NDA would drop to about 300. The House would shrink to 520 members, and the target would ease only slightly, to about 347. That would make the government’s task far harder.
The Shiv Sena (UBT) has challenged the merger of its six members with Shiv Sena in the Supreme Court, but the court declined to grant interim relief while it considers the matter.
The Upper House
In April, seven of AAP’s 10 Rajya Sabha members merged with the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP). The chairman accepted the merger, taking the BJP’s strength in the House to 113. The NDA has 141 members in the 245-member House, against the 163 needed, leaving it about 20 short. It would need help from opposition parties or walkouts.
If the bill clears both Houses, one more step may follow. Under Article 368, a constitutional amendment that changes the states’ representation in Parliament must also be ratified by at least half of the state legislatures.
What the Opposition wants
The Congress says it backs women’s reservation but doubts the government’s motives. It has demanded keeping the Lok Sabha at 543 seats, maintaining each state’s current number of seats, reserving 182 seats for women, and freezing the arrangement for 25 years. People aware of the matter said the opposition would support the bills if these were accepted, which would mean giving up the expansion plan. Rahul Gandhi, the leader of the Opposition in Lok Sabha, has called the amendment an attempt to seize power through delimitation and the redrawing of boundaries.
The government says it is confident. Shah on Thursday said that the government has the numbers.
If the bills fail to pass, there may not be enough time to hold the 2029 Lok Sabha election as per the new boundaries. That would push back both the expansion and the women’s quota.

Gauhati HC grants interim bail to former APSC chief accused in cash for job case
The court granted bail to Rakesh Paul on November 23 considering his prolonged incarceration, his wife’s medical condition (kidney failure) and delays in hearing of connected appeals
The Gauhati High Court granted interim bail of three months to former chairman of Assam Public Service Commission (APSC), who is serving a 14 year jail term in connection with a cash for job case.
A division bench of the court granted bail to Rakesh Paul on November 23 considering his prolonged incarceration, his wife’s medical condition (kidney failure) and delays in hearing of connected appeals. In his application, he had stated that both the kidneys of his wife have failed and needed transplant for which Paul needs to take care of her.
Paul has been in prison for over eight years now following his arrest in Nov 2016 for allegedly providing jobs to candidates appearing for the civil service exams in lieu of cash. He was released in March 2023 in connection with another case, but was arrested following conviction.
A division bench granted bail to Paul till February 28 next year or until disposal of his related criminal appeal, whichever happens earlier. It directed him to pay a bail bond of ₹1 lakh and three sureties of the like amount, one of who must own immovable property within the jurisdiction of the trial court where his case is being heard.
Also Read: Gauhati HC delivers split verdict on pleas to ban dog meat sale in Nagaland
It also imposed restrictions on his travel from within the jurisdiction of the trial court without obtaining prior permission.
The APSC cash-for-job case came to light in 2016 when many successful candidates including Assam Civil Service (ACS) and Assam Police Service (APS) officers who appeared in combined competitive exam (CCE) for years 2013 and 2014 were alleged to have indulged in irregular practices in cahoots with the then chairman Paul.
Following the revelations, police lodged several cases and arrested 60 serving officers from the CCE, 2013 batch. After detection of anomalies, 39 officers were terminated from service.
In April 2022, a special court in Guwahati framed charges against 67 accused in the job case. While 60 of them were applicants who appeared for the civil service exams, seven others were APSC members and officials including Paul. The trial in this case remains underway.
Following directions by the Gauhati High Court, the Assam government had formed two inquiry commissions to investigate the recruitments made through the CCEs of 2013 and 2014. The commission had submitted its report on the 2013 findings in April 2022 and the one on 2014 in October 2023.

“There is reason to believe that the candidates selected on extraneous considerations were allowed to write their examinations at places other than the examination hall or were allowed duplication. There is also reason to believe that the malpractices...pertaining to CCE 2013 but also pertaining to other examinations including CCE 2014 is quite bigger and larger than what could be unearthed in this inquiry and the criminal investigation,” the report for 2013, which was made public in February last year, read.
In July 2024, a special court in Guwahati sentenced Paul to 14 years imprisonment in connection with a separate case involving irregularities in recruitment of agriculture development officers (ADOs) and imposed a fine of ₹2 lakh. He had got bail in this case in March 2023, but was arrested again following the conviction.

Two other APSC members, Samedur Rahman and Basanta Kumar Doley, were convicted to 10 years each and imposed fines of ₹50,000. Twenty-nine others including Assistant District Prosecution Officers (ADPO) who got recruited using unfair means were sentenced to four years of imprisonment and fined ₹10,000 each.
The present case against the former APSC chairman and 43 others was lodged in 2017 following a complaint by an ADO job applicant alleging that Paul and others had asked for a bribe of ₹15 lakh to give him the job.

Coimbatore blast: Accused allowed 'A' Class facilities in prison, court cites ‘superior lifestyle’
Co-accused Navas was arrested in the case in October 2024 and is currently lodged at Central Prison, Coimbatore.
A Chennai court last week granted “A” class facilities inside the prison to an accused in the 2022 Coimbatore car bomb blast case, as it accepted his claim that his educational qualification and lifestyle entitled him to a superior category of accommodation in judicial custody and rejected the National Investigation Agency (NIA) objection.
An explosion occurred outside an ancient temple, “Arulmigu Kottai Sangameshwarar Thirukovil”, on Eswaran Kovil Street, Ukkadam, Coimbatore, on October 23, 2022. The vehicle-borne Improvised Explosives Device (V-IED) driven by the bomber Jamesha Mubeen exploded in front of the temple. Mubeen was killed in the blast.
Co-accused Navas was arrested in the case in October 2024 and is currently lodged at Central Prison, Coimbatore. He moved the special NIA court in Chennai under the New Tamil Nadu Prison Rules, 2024, seeking a direction to the Superintendent of Prisons, Central Prison, Coimbatore, to classify and provide him 'A' class facilities.
Under the New Tamil Nadu Prison Rules, 2024, a Class ‘A’ prisoner gets a better diet, bedding, books to read, newspapers, magazines, etc.
According to the November 17 court order, reviewed by HT, Navas argued that he is a graduate and an income tax assessee, and that he has completed the Master of Business Administration at Bharathiar University, Coimbatore, in April 2020.
He submitted that under Rule 804 of the Tamil Nadu Prison Manual (The new Tamil Nadu Prison Rules 2024), undertrial prisoners shall be of two classes: special and ordinary. The special class, he argued, citing the rule, shall consist of those who by special status, education and habit of life have “been accustomed to a superior mode of living”.
Navas told the court that he is “accustomed to a superior mode of living” and that he “shall be eligible for ‘A Class’ (Special Class) by social status, education or habit of life”.
The NIA opposed his plea, saying he attempted to mislead the court by submitting income-tax payment receipts to establish his eligibility for special-class facilities. It pointed out that Navas had paid only ₹1,000 in tax for each of the assessment years 2025-26 and 2026-27 and that he had not disclosed his source of income. The agency argued that merely being an income-tax assessee doesn’t entitle Navas to special-class facilities.
The judge, however, rejected the NIA’s objections. Citing Navas’s educational qualification certificates, the judge stated:...it is evident that Navas is having education and habit of life accustomed to a superior mode of living”.
“Considering his superior mode of living, Navas is eligible for Special Class in the prison,” the court said.
Investigations revealed that the blast was carried out by an Islamic State-inspired module comprising Jameesha Mubeen, Mohammed Azarudeen, Umar Faaruq, Sheikh Hidayathullah and Sanofer Ali. The accused persons conspired to carry out a series of suicidal terror attacks in Coimbatore city following a conspiracy hatched in the forested area of the Sathyamangalam region in Erode district of Tamil Nadu.
Mubeen was allegedly inspired by the bayans (sermons) of Zahran Hashim, a radical Islamic cleric of Sri Lanka, who masterminded the Easter serial suicide bomb attacks in 2019, killing around 260 people. Mubeen wanted to orchestrate a similar kind of attack against the ‘kafirs’ in India.

BJD MP urges Centre to monitor airfares, add flights to Odisha ahead of New Year
Sasmit Patra cited Trip.com data showing fares rising from ₹17,622 in July to ₹24,236 in October.
Biju Janata Dal (BJD) MP Sasmit Patra on Thursday urged Union civil aviation minister Kinjarapu Rammohan Naidu to intervene over steep airfares on routes connecting Odisha with major cities, seeking fare monitoring and additional flights ahead of the New Year 2027.
“The recurring high airfare escalation on routes connecting Odisha, particularly Bhubaneswar and Jharsuguda, with Delhi, Mumbai, Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Chennai, Kolkata and Pune during festivals, summer vacations and winter breaks is very painful to the thousands of students, families and professionals from Odisha,” Patra wrote in a letter to the minister on November 26.
Citing historical fare data, Patra said Delhi-Bhubaneswar return fares averaged ₹14,032 in February, compared with ₹19,294 in October—an increase of around 37.5 per cent, according to KAYAK. He also cited Trip.com data showing fares rising from ₹17,622 in July to ₹24,236 in October. Ahead of Diwali 2026, Bengaluru-Jharsuguda nonstop fares reportedly increased from ₹4,200 to ₹16,200—nearly a 286 per cent increase, he added, citing a Moneycontrol report.
Patra also flagged a decline in air connectivity to the state, saying Bhubaneswar’s domestic destinations reportedly fell from 29 in 2025 to 19 in 2026, despite the airport handling 5.1 million passengers in 2025-26.
Referring to a previous intervention by the civil aviation ministry, Patra said the deployment of 1,750 additional flights across 100 sectors during the October 2025 festive season had helped moderate airfares.
“This shows intervention by your Ministry in the past has helped moderate the fare,” he wrote.
He also referred to the 353rd report of the Parliamentary Standing Committee, dated August 10, 2023, which recommended festive-season fare monitoring, reasonable upper fare caps and transparency in fare categories.
“Yet the DGCA monitors only 78 routes monthly, covering approximately 27 per cent of domestic traffic,” Patra added.
Urging the minister to ensure monitoring of fares on Odisha-bound flights during the approaching winter vacations, Patra said thousands of students, families and professionals travelling home for the winter break and New Year should not be adversely affected.
“Please deploy more aircraft if you have to; just ensure that the airfares stay moderate as you did during the October 2025 festive season,” he further wrote.

Sanjay Maurya is a Principal Correspondent with Hindustan Times, where he covers education, with a focus on school and higher education, competitive examinations, education policy and governance. Working as part of the National Bureau, he is based in New Delhi and reports on the Ministry of Education and covers various statutory bodies like UGC, AICTE and NCTE and autonomous bodies like CBSE and NCERT. His reporting also tracks the implementation of key government reforms and policies from school education to higher education including in IITs, NITs, IIMs, central and state universities, and their impact on students and educational institutions. His reporting on the irregularities and rushed implementation of CBSE's On-Screen Marking (OSM) system for evaluation of Class 12 board exams 2026, triggered administrative action, leading to the transfer of the board's two senior-most officials and the constitution of a committee to probe alleged irregularities in procurement process of the system. He joined Hindustan Times in December 2024. Prior to that, he had a three-year stint at Careers360, where he reported on school and higher education, entrance examinations, admissions, rankings and various education policies involving universities and professional education bodies. Over the years, Maurya has reported extensively on major developments in India's education sector, including the implementation of the National Education Policy (NEP) 2020, reforms in the National Testing Agency (NTA) following the NEET-UG 2024 controversy, changes in school education, higher education regulation, and the evolution of entrance examinations such as NEET, JEE and CUET. He regularly produces data-driven and explanatory stories based on government documents, parliamentary proceedings, court records and official data. His focus remains on helping readers understand how education policies and institutional decisions affect millions of students, teachers and educational institutions across the country.
Parliament consultative committee discusses foreign campuses, student exchanges
Pralhad Joshi pointed to demand for CBSE schools abroad, saying it demonstrated the “credibility of Indian education programmes and potential for scalability at global level”
Union education minister Pralhad Joshi on Wednesday chaired the first meeting of the Parliamentary Consultative Committee on Education for 2026, with discussions focusing on taking Indian universities overseas, facilitating foreign university campuses in India and attracting international students to the country.
The meeting, held on November 25, was centred on the theme of “Internationalisation of Indian Education” and positioning India as a “global knowledge hub”.
In a post on X after the meeting, Joshi said, “Deliberations covered expanding Indian universities globally, facilitating foreign university campuses in India, strengthening international research partnerships, student and faculty exchange programmes, and attracting international students.”
He also said members were sensitised about measures to internationalise school education through Central Board of School Education (CBSE) Global and National Institute of Open Schooling (NIOS) expansion, multilingual learning, global teacher mobility, curriculum reforms and cross-cultural exposure.

He also pointed to the demand for CBSE schools abroad, saying it demonstrated the “credibility of Indian education programmes and their potential for scalability at the global level”.
On school education, the Department of School Education and Literacy (DoSEL) highlighted curriculum alignment with global standards, multilingual education, student and teacher exchange programmes and the role of the national assessment centre Performance Assessment, Review, and Analysis of Knowledge for Holistic Development (PARAKH) in academic equivalence and quality alignment.
It informed the committee that 268 CBSE-affiliated schools were functioning across 26 countries, with an overseas regional office in Dubai. A “standardised assessment framework” had also been implemented across affiliated schools globally to ensure uniformity, the ministry said in a press statement.
Addressing the committee, Joshi highlighted the historical global influence of the Indian Knowledge System (IKS) and said the ministry’s objective was to further expand its global footprint. He said steps were being taken to establish campuses of Indian higher education institutions (HEIs) overseas and facilitate foreign universities in setting up campuses in India.
Also Read: India’s continuing tradition of celebrating its teachers
The minister informed the members that around 21 foreign HEIs were currently operational in India, apart from joint academic and research collaborations.
The Department of Higher Education (DoHE) of the Union education ministry outlined four strategies for internationalisation: academic and research collaborations; attracting international students to study in India; allowing foreign higher education institutions to establish branch campuses in India; and enabling Indian institutions to set up campuses abroad.
Parliamentary Consultative Committee on Education
The Parliamentary Consultative Committee for the ministry of education is an informal platform that brings together MPs and the government to discuss the ministry’s policies, programmes and their implementation. Its purpose is to provide lawmakers an opportunity to understand the government’s work and offer suggestions on policy matters.
According to the Ministry of Parliamentary Affairs’ guidelines, the objectives of such committees include “promote informal consultation between Members of Parliament and the Government” and provide the government an opportunity to benefit from MPs’ advice and guidance.

Oscar fees can be 'prohibitive', says Academy official at IFFI in Goa
For independent and regional filmmakers in India, many of whom work on small budgets, even the lower rate is a big sum.
Indian filmmakers chasing an Oscar should look beyond the international feature film category, Natalie Wade, a senior official of the Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences said at the 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI) in Goa. She admitted that the cost of competing for the award can be too high for many filmmakers outside the US.
Wade, vice president, member relations and awards administration at the Academy, was speaking at a masterclass at the festival during which filmmakers, students and academics asked why Indian cinema, one of the largest film industries in the world, still struggles to find a place at the Oscars.
‘High fee is prohibitive’
Wade admitted that the cost of competing for an Oscar can keep many filmmakers out. Submitting a film is free, but filmmakers face a $25,000 ( ₹23,13,191) fee. Wade said the Academy also has an alternate rate of $8,000 ( ₹7,40,221), but added, “I think we can still say that it can be prohibitive as well.”
For independent and regional filmmakers in India, many of whom work on small budgets, even the lower rate is a big sum. Asked whether the Academy could charge a sliding fee depending on the region a filmmaker comes from, as many international academic conferences do, Wade called it "a great suggestion." "Our committees evaluate the rules on a yearly basis. So what exists now may not exist, you know, for the next cycle," she said.
Her remarks come as the Oscars continue to face criticism for being Anglo and Eurocentric. The #OscarsSoWhite controversy of 2015 forced the Academy to diversify its membership, but the international feature category is still largely dominated by European films. In nearly seven decades, only three Indian films have been nominated in the category - 'Mother India', 'Salaam Bombay' and 'Lagaan'. None of them won. Indian filmmakers in the masterclass audience spoke about the pressure to cut songs or change their storytelling to suit Western audiences.
Lack of diversity in Academy
According to Wade, about 75% of the Academy's members are from the US and only 25% from the rest of the world, with around 60 Indian members. She agreed that this was not enough. "I think it is not enough and we're doing what we can as an organisation because we are wanting to be a global organisation," she said.
Wade said Indian filmmakers often wrongly believe that the international feature category is their only way in. "If an Indian film is not selected by the selection committee, they can enter our general entry and best picture categories. So I would highly encourage films to choose that pathway," she said. She said international films had competed across categories last year, and she advised filmmakers to get in touch with Indian Academy members, who can sponsor them as candidates for membership.
Indian movies in Oscars
Every year, India's official entry for the international feature category is chosen by a selection committee of the Film Federation of India, and the choice often sparks debate. Critics have accused the committee of overlooking films with strong international buzz. In 2022, it picked the Gujarati film ‘Chhello Show’ over SS Rajamouli's RRR. RRR's makers then campaigned on their own in the general categories, and its song ‘Naatu Naatu’ went on to win the Oscar. In 2024, the committee's choice of ‘Laapataa Ladies’ over Payal Kapadia's Cannes Grand Prix winner ‘All We Imagine As Light’ drew sharp criticism.
Asked whether IFFI could become an Oscar-qualifying festival, Wade said festivals can apply for the status. The Academy already recognises several qualifying festivals across the world, but IFFI is not one of them yet.
On artificial intelligence (AI), a question that is troubling the film world, Wade said the Academy stands firmly with human creativity. "The academy is determined to champion filmmakers and the human artistry at the heart of filmmaking," she said. She said the award rules have an AI clause at the beginning, and that one factor is how far a human authored the project. Each branch's executive committee decides how this applies to its own categories.
She also said films released only on OTT platforms will not be considered without a theatrical release in the US. "We do not anticipate this changing anytime soon. The theatrical release is close to our members' hearts," she said.
Wade said the 100th Academy Awards, taking place in March 2028 will be a global celebration, with efforts planned around the world, and that the ceremony will introduce a new category for stunt design. Wade said her favourite Indian film is SS Rajamouli's RRR.

articles.text:
‘Delimitation makes MPs’ work easier’: Rebel TMC MP Kakoli Ghosh ahead of House sitting
Kakoli Ghosh Dastidar, said the TMC rebel group will decide its stance after seeing the bill but added that delimitation will make lawmakers’ work easier.
The 20 rebel Trinamool Congress (TMC) MPs, whose proposed merger with the little-known Nationalist Citizens Party of India (NCPI) is yet to receive the Lok Sabha Speaker’s approval, could hold the key to the fate of the delimitation Bill if it is tabled during Parliament’s four-day special sitting.
In an interview with HT, one of the dissidents, MP Kakoli Ghosh Dastidar, said the group will decide its stance after seeing the bill but added that delimitation will make lawmakers’ work easier. Edited excerpts:
Q: What is your reaction to the special session being called?
There was an expectation, because the Monsoon Session had not been prorogued. Usually, after a session ends, the date for the next one is announced, and 14 days' notice is required. Knowing how these official processes work, we knew there might be another special session. We were only waiting for the date, which wasn't announced until today.
Q: Have you received any formal briefing on the agenda?
Deep Dive
Not yet. Maybe that will happen on the morning of the 30th. If it has already happened, we haven't received it. We have only seen the post by Parliamentary Affairs Minister Kiren Rijiju, which was forwarded to our group. Naturally, we are preparing to travel.
Q: Has the government or the NDA approached you informally on delimitation?
We have not been formally notified about the business to be held. We know it is government business, but the exact nature has not been told to us. Maybe there is still time. As we receive that information, we will decide.
Q: The Speaker has not ruled on the disqualification petitions or the merger. Will you be allowed to vote?
As members, we have every right to vote. But we were given separate sittings in the last session.
Q: Does separate sitting mean your vote counts with your previous party or with the new one?
That will be decided by the Honourable Speaker.
Q: If it is a Constitution Amendment Bill and a delimitation Bill, has your party decided whether to support it?
Let us cross that bridge when we come to it, because we don't know what Bill is coming. Discussion has been going on. In April, we discussed and debated the delimitation Bill. I feel this is a constitutional provision that depends on the census and population, and it is always wise to go by the constitutional provision. After delimitation, the work of MPs becomes much easier, because it gives you a number of constituents you can really approach. Governance becomes easy. The country's population has also increased, and the forefathers wrote in the Constitution that these things should happen in a certain year. So we are following that.
Q: Any message for the voters of Bengal? People will want to know whether they lose or gain political weight under the new scheme.
We will say that only when we debate and when we come to know what the Bill is. We don't even know what Bill is coming. The notification does not mention the name of the Bill. It says only "government business". Once we are told, we will definitely discuss it.

‘Poor’ air

articles.text:
More women in judiciary will make society more fair: President Draupadi Murmu
President Draupadi Murmu on Thursday said that greater participation of women in the judiciary can make society more inclusive and add balance and diversity to judicial decision-making process
President Draupadi Murmu on Thursday said that greater participation of women in the judiciary can make society more inclusive and add balance and diversity to judicial decision-making process.
Addressing a gathering of Supreme Court judges, former CJIs, judges, lawyers and law students at the Constitution Day function organised by the Supreme Court here, President Murmu said, “Larger and more active participation of women in the bench and Bar will help make our society more fair, just, equitable and inclusive.”
Emphasising how the role of women can add diversity to the decision-making process, she cited the example of Hansaben Mehta, a former member of the Constituent Assembly that framed our Constitution, who was instrumental in amending Article 1 of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR). In 1947-48, when the text of UDHR was drafted, Mehta took part in the deliberations as a delegate from India. The opening Article which said, “All men are born free and equal,” was changed to “All human beings” at Mehta’s instance.
“A woman’s perspective can add to inclusion, diversity and balance to judicial decision-making,” the President said, adding, “Women have made valuable contributions to the jurisprudence in our country. We should encourage greater participation of women as judges and lawyers.”
The President was accompanied by the Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant and Union Law Minister Arjun Ram Meghwal, the key stakeholders in ensuring the appointment of judges to constitutional courts. She said, “Greater emphasis on inclusivity and merit will further strengthen our judiciary.”
She congratulated the government for making India “Naxal-free” and urged the judiciary to consider the reasons that make innocent villagers become Naxals. “When I see the faces of surrendered people who are Naxals, they look innocent. Those who are inside have made them so. Why were they made Naxals? We need to work on this.”
Highlighting another area of concern, the President said that schools, during her time, allowed students of all strata of society to study, play and interact together. However, today, she stated that this situation has changed, where the elite send their children to good, private schools while a poor child gets to study in a government-run school.
“Children are not poor, only their parents are poor. This mentality of the child that I am poor and so I cannot aspire to study in a good school cannot help a child progress... Children are the future of this country and for the sake of the country’s future, all children must get education on the same terms,” she said.
She also urged the leading advocates in the legal profession to inspire the upcoming, young lawyers by presenting shining examples of how excellence can be blended with empathy and competence with compassion.
Mixing Hindi and English in the text of her speech, the President said that the legal curriculum taught across law universities should give as much emphasis to “empathy and ethics” as to the instruction on law. She also spoke about the need to ensure justice reaches all people and that the poor and marginalised avail of free legal aid for better access to justice.
A People’s Court
CJI Surya Kant sharing his views on the occasion said that the Supreme Court, once looked upon as a place only few could afford to access, has now emerged as a “people’s court”. “That era is now over, for even the most eminent among them must appear on exactly the same footing as a lawyer from a small town, bound by the same queue, the same clock, and the same rules,” CJI said.
He said that over the years, the judges of the top court have “laboured long to make this court, in the fullest sense, the people’s court.” Access to court is governed by a system, not status, he said, adding, “Privilege finds little room within it (system), and it is in this quiet, everyday work, far more than in any proclamation, that a people’s court is truly sustained.”
He also quoted from Hansaben Mehta’s speech in the Constituent Assembly in 1946 where she drew a distinction between “privilege” and “justice”. CJI said, “This distinction lies at the very heart of our Constitution, which was conceived not as a charter of advantage for a fortunate few, but as a covenant of justice with every citizen.”
To this end, he said that the court has prioritised the hearing of cases concerning persons with disabilities, survivors of acid attacks, senior citizens aged above 80, families below the poverty line, or litigants who come through legal aid, who can least afford to wait.

Union home minister Amit Shah on Thursday underlined the importance and need to uphold the spirit of the Constitution, while highlighting the Bharatiya Janata Party’s (BJP) commitment to providing 33% reservation to women in Parliament. Describing it as one of the positive constitutional amendments, Shah said that Congress was blocking its implementation but would not be able to stop them.
Addressing the Samvidhan Gaurav Diwas programme in New Delhi, Shah said Prime Minister Narendra Modi had instituted the observance of Constitution Day in 2015 to take the constitutional values of justice, liberty, equality and fraternity to every citizen. The aim, he said, was to ensure that the Constitution’s spirit was understood and strengthened among students, youth and citizens, rather than treating it merely as a guide to governance.
Shah also spoke about the Uniform Civil Code (UCC), noting that the Constitution’s framers had included it in the Directive Principles of State Policy. He said the UCC would be implemented in all BJP-governed states.
The Constitution, Shah said, was not merely a document to govern the country but embodied the aspirations, sacrifices and values of those who fought for India’s freedom. The home minister and senior BJP leader accused the Congress of undermining constitutional institutions, curtailing fundamental rights during the Emergency and repeatedly amending the Constitution to suit its political interests.
“Those who wave the Constitution merely for show should take some time to understand its true spirit. The Constitution is the roadmap to reclaim our lost pride. The Constitution of India is not merely a legal document; it is a reflection of the dreams and aspirations of the freedom fighters who made sacrifices during the 90-year-long freedom struggle,” he said.
Shah said every citizen had a responsibility to work towards the goal of a Viksit and Aatmanirbhar Bharat by 2047, as set by Prime Minister Narendra Modi. He then recounted an anecdote about a Congress parliamentarian who, during a discussion in Parliament, asked whether Modi would be there in 2047.
“The Congress MP asked me if Modi ji would be there. I told them that they are focusing on an individual. Our sights are on Bharat Mata, and Bharat will be there in 2047,” Shah said.
Shah said the UCC would be implemented in all BJP-ruled states in the coming days. Accusing the opposition of spreading misconceptions about the Constitution even as the country earned recognition and acclaim across the world, he said: “I want to tell them today that the UCC was envisaged by the makers of our Constitution and included in its Directive Principles of State Policy. Every citizen of this country should have the right to live under one common law, irrespective of religion, whether Hindu, Sikh, Muslim, Christian or Parsi. Since its inception, the Bharatiya Janata Party has maintained that the country should be governed by a Uniform Civil Code. Laws should not be framed on the basis of religion. This is a position that Rahul ji’s party outrightly rejects. But today, I have come to state clearly that in the coming days, we will implement the UCC in every state governed by a BJP government.”
Referring to the historic amendments the BJP had brought to the Constitution, Shah mentioned the Goods and Services Tax and reservations for economically weaker sections and women. He said his party was committed to guaranteeing 33% reservation for women, which he said the Congress was blocking.
“Through the 106th Constitutional Amendment, we provided for 33% reservation for women in Parliament and state legislative assemblies. The Congress party is sitting on this and blocking its implementation. I want to tell Rahul ji today that it is the resolve of the Bharatiya Janata Party and our leader Narendra Modi that women of this country will get 33% reservation, come what may. “Rahul Gandhi, who speaks about the Constitution, goes abroad and indulges in the act of defaming India. You come from a Congress party that, by imposing the Emergency for 18 months, effectively put the spirit of the Constitution under lock and key,” he said.
Shah also said former Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru was the first to suppress freedom of expression in the Constitution by inserting Article 19(2) into Article 19.
“The Congress and BJP both parties have amended the Constitution, but the objective behind their respective amendments was different,” he said.

The foreign nationals were allegedly held captive and forced to dupe people in their home countries through cyber frauds after being trafficked into India
The 164 Indonesian and Malaysian nationals rescued from a fake international call centre in Noida, will be repatriated to their respective countries through the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) and the Foreigners Regional Registration Office (FRRO) after the completion of requisite legal formalities, two senior police officers said.
The foreign nationals were allegedly held captive and forced to dupe people in their home countries through cyber frauds after being trafficked into India.
Police will inform both the MEA and FRRO about the rescued foreigners and seek their assistance in finding a suitable accommodation in the city where they can stay until repatriation procedures are complete and they are flown back, the officers said, adding that the embassies of both countries will also be involved in the entire process.
“Since all 164 rescued foreigners are victims of an organised human trafficking syndicate and alleged cyber slavery, none of them will face any adverse legal action. Their medical examination was conducted and they will now be handed over to the FRRO, which will ensure their safe accommodation and return to their respective countries through the MEA’s intervention,” one of the officers cited above said.
On Thursday, the Delhi Police crime branch said the Malaysian and Indonesian nationals were busy carrying out cyber fraud activities when its inter-state cell (ISC) team raided the fake call centre running on the sixth floor of a multi-storey commercial tower in Noida Sector-136, Uttar Pradesh, on Wednesday night.
A 25-year-old Malaysian national, identified as Tan Guan Wei, was arrested for allegedly running the operation on behalf of two Indian handlers, Sunil Kumar and Sushil Kumar, both of whom remain absconding. One of the two is suspected to be based in Malaysia, said joint commissioner of police (crime) Surender Kumar.
“The rescued foreigners claimed they had been trafficked into India on the pretext of employment and other lucrative opportunities. They all were flown to India on business visas. The cyber syndicate members seized their passports soon after their arrival. We recovered their passports from a locker belonging to the manager of the call centre who is also absconding. There were a total of 174 passports (95 Indonesian and 79 Malaysian). While 164 nationals of the two countries were rescued and one Malaysian was arrested, we are trying to find out where the remaining 9 (three Indonesians and seven Malaysians) are,” said Kumar.
Police said the victims were trafficked into Delhi over the past four months. They were allegedly confined in a 65-room PG accommodation within a six-storey residential building in Noida, which the two absconding Indian handlers, Sunil and Sushil, had rented for ₹12.24 lakh per month. Their movements were restricted and their access to phones controlled, police said.

Members of the network allegedly assaulted those who resisted or refused to participate in the fraudulent activities to ensure compliance. The victims were not allowed to leave the PG under any circumstances. They were occasionally permitted to speak to their families back home, but only under close supervision of those running the racket, a senior police officer, associated with the operation, said..
“The victims were also served substandard food and forced to follow written scripts to cheat unsuspecting people in Indonesia and Malaysia through fraudulent investment platforms. They were tortured, harassed and threatened,” the officer added.
Police said the trafficked foreigners were trained to participate in cyber fraud and forced to communicate with prospective targets using mobile phones, computers and SIM cards recovered during the police raids. The syndicate allegedly used fraudulent online platforms, websites and APK-based applications, including Zenttrix and Quantvoro, to target unsuspecting people in Indonesia and Malaysia.
“The modus operandi involved creating fictitious female identities and online profiles to approach prospective victims through social media and other communication platforms. The operators allegedly developed online relationships, gained the confidence of victims and subsequently induced them to invest money through fraudulent trading and investment platforms,” joint CP Kumar said.

articles.text:
Karn Pratap Singh has been writing on crime, policing, and issues of safety in Delhi for almost a decade. He covers high-intensity spot news, including terror strikes, serial blasts and security threats in the national capital.
92 Indonesians, 72 Malaysians lured to Delhi, forced to work for no pay in scam call centre
The network is among the first of its kind busts in India involving foreign nationals allegedly trafficked into the country.
A total of 164 foreign nationals from Indonesia and Malaysia have been rescued after Delhi Police busted what officials described as a “cyber slavery and human trafficking network” – akin to syndicates operating in southeast Asia where Indians are generally forced to work in cyber-scam compounds – operating out of a fake international call centre in Noida, officials said Thursday. A Malaysian national was arrested.
The syndicate lured people to India with false job promises, confined them in a paying guest (PG) accommodation and forced them to participate in cyber fraud targeting people in their home countries without any pay, the people cited above said.
The network is among the first of its kind busts in India involving foreign nationals allegedly trafficked into the country and forced into cyber fraud, joint commissioner of police (crime) Surender Kumar said.
Deep Dive
Of the 164 people rescued, 92 are Indonesian nationals and 72 are Malaysian. They were allegedly confined to a 65-room PG in Noida and made to work at a fake call centre operating from a commercial building in Sector 136. Their passports were seized after they arrived in India, their movements restricted and their access to phones controlled, police said.
Those who resisted or refused to participate in the fraudulent activities were allegedly assaulted by members of the network to ensure compliance, a senior police officer said. The victims were not allowed to leave the PG and were occasionally permitted to speak to their families back home, but only under close supervision of those running the racket, officers said.
The victims were also served substandard food and forced to follow written scripts to cheat unsuspecting people in Indonesia and Malaysia through fraudulent investment platforms, police said.
A 25-year-old Malaysian national, identified as Tan Guan Wei, has been arrested for allegedly running the operation on behalf of two Indian handlers, Sunil Kumar and Sushil Kumar, both of whom remain absconding. One of the two is suspected to be based in Malaysia, police said.
Wei arrived in India around four months ago on a business visa, allegedly at the direction of the two handlers. His role was to train the Indonesian and Malaysian recruits, prepare the scripts they had to read while making fraudulent calls, the joint CP said.
The two Indian handlers had been running the fake call centre under the guise of a private firm named SKV Enterprises. They had rented a commercial facility on the sixth floor of a high-rise building in Sector 136, where the call centre had been operating for around three months, and a six-storey residential building housing the victims. “The accused were paying ₹20.24 lakh per month as rent for the commercial and residential facilities,” Kumar said. The call centre’s monthly rent was ₹8 lakh, while the 65-room PG cost ₹12.24 lakh a month, he added.
Subsequent raids at the call centre and the PG accommodation led to the recovery of 355 mobile phones, 168 desktop computers, 26 laptops, 63 SIM cards, including 31 international cards, and 174 Indonesian and Malaysian passports, Kumar said.
A case has been registered at the crime branch police station under sections of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) relating to abduction, human trafficking, exploitation of trafficked persons, unlawful compulsory labour, wrongful confinement, cheating by personation, criminal intimidation and criminal conspiracy. The sections invoked include 138, 143, 144, 146, 127, 318, 319, 351, 61 and 3 of the BNS.
Police have issued look-out circulars against Sunil and Sushil, and raids are underway to arrest them. Sushil is believed to be in India, Kumar said.
The case comes against the backdrop of growing concerns over human trafficking into cyber-scam compounds in southeast Asia. Nearly 7,000 Indian nationals were rescued from cyber-scam compounds and fake job rackets in Cambodia, Laos and Myanmar, according to data shared by the Centre in Parliament in February.

The Delhi High Court has dismissed 14 revision petitions and upheld charges against Former Railway Minister Lalu Prasad Yadav and 13 other accused persons, including Rabri Devi, Tejaswi Prasad Yadav, Prem Chand Gupta, and Sarla Gupta. They had challenged the order of charges passed by the Special CBI Court on October 13, 2025.
Special CBI Judge had framed charges against the petitioners for offences punishable under Section 120B read with Section 420 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860, and Section 13(2) read with Section 13(1)(d) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988.
Justice Swarana Kanta Sharma dismissed the revision petitions on Thursday and upheld the order on charges and said there is no infirmity in the order passed by the trial court.
While rejecting the revisions, Justice Swarana Kanta Sharma said, " This Court finds no infirmity in the impugned order dated 13.10.2025 passed by the learned Special Court. The material on record, considered in its entirety, discloses sufficient grounds to proceed against the accused persons, i.e. petitioners herein, for the offences for which charges have been framed against each of them."
"The impugned order does not call for any interference by this Court in exercise of its revisional jurisdiction. The impugned order dated 13.10.2025 is upheld," Justice Sharma said in the judgement.
The bench said, "A conspiracy rarely unfolds in the open. It is woven through separate acts, divided among different hands, and is revealed only when the threads are seen together."
The High Court said that the material placed before this Court prima facie indicates the involvement of Lalu Prasad Yadav in the policy decisions concerning the budget hotels and the BNR Hotels at the time when the process leading to their award was underway.
It is alleged that Lalu Prasad Yadav, while serving as Minister of Railways, had entered into a criminal conspiracy with the Kochhar brothers of M/s Sujata Hotel Pvt. Ltd. and others.

PM solar rooftop scheme nears 7mn household installations; target of 10mn by March 27
PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana was launched in February 2024 and gives subsidies up to ₹78,000 to households for installing a 3KW solar panel
The Centre’s flagship solar rooftop scheme, PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana, is nearing installations in seven million households, having released nearly ₹38,000 crore in subsidies across the country, the latest data from the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE) shows.
The scheme, which has a target of covering ten million households by the end of March 2027, is on track, officials said, adding it is also gaining momentum with the help of a recently launched QR-based tool, meant to simplify installation for users. The tool has recorded over 4,50,000 clicks in the last three months, since its launch, data showed.
PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana was launched in February 2024 and gives subsidies up to ₹78,000 to households for installing a 3KW solar panel.
Reviewing the scheme earlier this month, Prime Minister Narendra Modi at the launch of the Bharat Renewable Energy (BRE) Summit and Expo 2026 in Delhi on November 2 had said the scheme was now covering nearly 1,00,000 new homes every six days. He also said the scheme had cut electricity bills by roughly 76%.

The latest data showed as of November 26, 6.91 million households have covered, with ₹37,989 crore released as subsidy. The total installed solar rooftop capacity across the country through this scheme stood at 20.2 GW till November 26.
The ministry had on August 20 this year also launched a QR-code based interactive tool to address any bottlenecks and simplify solar installation for households. Government data shows the QR-code portal has logged 4,57,561 scans in three months.

articles.title: The token factory never sleeps
articles.text:
Agentic AI has supercharged demand for inference infrastructure. According to Goldman Sachs, token consumption is set to jump 24-fold to 120 quadrillion tokens per month between this year and 2030. Enterprises, wary of frontier model sticker shock, are now building their own GPU estates to cope.

Those enterprises shouldn't blindly follow hyperscalers' lead when taking AI inference kit into production. The indicators of success for such companies are different than those for a frontier model provider, and so are the constraints. DIY AI infrastructure at the enterprise level has to earn ROI quickly, meaning that enterprises must focus on sustained operation. That makes engineering criteria such as uptime, heat and power, service windows, and deployment times doubly important. The performance benchmarks that hyperscalers focus on won't matter nearly as much to the average bank or retailer.

ASUS is presenting the ASUS NVIDIA HGX Rubin System, built on the NVIDIA HGX Rubin NVL8 platform, as a worked example of sustained AI inference infrastructure. It announced two models at NVIDIA GTC Berlin in October: the 3U hybrid-cooled XR R1I12B-M1BHFS and the 2U fully liquid-cooled XR R1I12B-M1BLFS.

Agents change the compute bill

Agents represent a hockey stick curve for token consumption because an agent isn't a single prompt. It loops until the job's done, often spawning other versions of itself in the process. This is how it breaks a goal into steps and works through them iteratively.

While training is a batch workload, agent inference is a production service that runs around the clock and only gets bigger. NVIDIA is making each generation of systems more powerful than the last to keep up with the demands of both.

Running at scale, day after day, is another matter. A useful way to think about the infrastructure that does it is as a token factory: it takes in power, data and GPU compute and turns out tokens. What counts is throughput, meaning how many tokens, and how many users, the same power and floor space can serve, hour after hour.

Enterprises move from pilots to AI factories

Enterprises are moving ahead quickly with their AI factory projects. According to Deloitte's AI infrastructure survey, published in March, 64 percent of respondents have started limited or at-scale AI factory deployments, while 88 percent expect to do so by 2028. They are spending more on AI infrastructure to do it: 86 percent expect their budgets to increase over the next three years.

Enterprises have different problems from hyperscalers and frontier model companies, though. Model builders often get to design greenfield campuses around their GPUs. Conversely, enterprises are often working with small operations teams in existing datacenters that may not have been built with AI in mind. That means they need to think harder about maintenance windows, existing management tooling and predictable deployment. And they'll often be retrofitting halls whose racks rarely draw more than 30 kW.

In token factory terms, the ASUS NVIDIA HGX Rubin System is the core compute engine. Each system puts eight NVIDIA HGX Rubin GPUs on the NVIDIA HGX Rubin NVL8 platform, linked by sixth-generation NVLink. ASUS has designed its equipment to support the constraints above. Its customers can choose between the hybrid and fully liquid-cooled models, and they can opt for partial or full rack configurations by buying multiple trays. This enables them to match their facilities' needs.

Peak performance versus sustained performance

The other difference between model providers and enterprises lies in which numbers they care about. Peak performance is different from sustained performance. The first is a specification sheet number, while the second is what the GPU actually delivers hours into a heavy workload.

Production inference tends to run continuously, especially when it uses agents, as opposed to training, which is a sporadic job. So the sustained figure is the one that buyers pay for. Heat becomes a real issue here because when cooling can't keep up, GPUs throttle their clocks to protect themselves. In a token factory, a throttled GPU is a slower production line.

The more advanced the architecture becomes, the higher the stakes get. NVIDIA HGX Rubin GPU has raised them to their highest point, delivering up to 400 petaflops of NVFP4 inference per eight-GPU board, according to NVIDIA's sparse specification. This is screamingly fast, but the increased heat per board means less margin before throttling.

ASUS designed both models to put direct-to-chip liquid cooling on every GPU. Only the 3U unit leaves the CPUs on air cooling. ASUS also says it puts every configuration through a 168-hour stress test.

Power and heat set the shape of the rack

As boards increase their compute density, pushing up the power and heat requirements, planning naturally has to move out of the server room and into the facility. That's the case whether you're talking about an entire NVL72 rack or a stack of eight-GPU servers like the ASUS systems.

There are other things to consider beyond heat. Few datacenters run racks drawing more than 30 kilowatts, says the Uptime Institute. Yet a single liquid-cooled tray of the ASUS systems draws up to 23.9 kilowatts, and a full rack of nine has a power budget of about 216 kilowatts.

Floor loading and power distribution matter as much as cooling.

NVIDIA HGX Rubin GPU raises the stakes again. The eight-GPU format enables organizations to buy their computing power in more granular steps. That's where the two ASUS systems come into their own. With few enterprises needing a training cluster at NVL72 scale, the advantage is that an HGX box lets them buy AI compute in digestible pieces.

The ASUS systems also come with a 54V busbar and cable-free board-to-board design. ASUS says this simplifies assembly and improves reliability.

Connectivity, storage and management

So that's space, power and heat. But a GPU board won't produce many tokens if the network, storage or operational tooling can't feed it properly. Agent workloads move context and data all the time, so east-west bandwidth and local storage are key to effective utilization. Any new equipment should ideally slot straight into the enterprise's existing management and monitoring tooling.

ASUS ships the whole rack, including servers, networking, power and storage, as a single blueprint. ASUS pre-validates this AI Factory reference architecture at rack scale so that organizations can plan for future growth. That includes dedicated management nodes and a management switch.

Inside each tray, ASUS has sized the data paths to keep the GPUs fed. Eight OSFP ports on NVIDIA ConnectX-9 give every GPU 800Gb/s of east-west bandwidth to the rest of the cluster, and an NVIDIA BlueField-4 DPU adds two 400GbE ports. Within the board, the eight GPUs talk to each other over NVLink at 3,600GB/s, ASUS says. The 2U tray takes up to 4TB of DDR5 system memory and has eight E1.S NVMe bays for fast local data access, while the 3U model offers a choice of U.2 or E1.S drives.

Built to be serviced

The other issue for enterprises putting AI inference into production is service and maintenance. In a liquid-cooled box, routine fixes can mean draining a coolant loop, which is downtime, and lost token output, that most enterprises can't afford, especially when dealing with non-batch workloads such as inferencing. So ASUS set out to make components quicker to swap.

On the 2U fully liquid-cooled model, ASUS did it with independent, tool-less CPU and GPU sleds, each with its own direct-to-chip cooling. On the 3U hybrid, ASUS says the air-cooled CPU sled cuts maintenance time by up to 50 percent.

From loading dock to first token

Services aren't just about server maintenance. They're also about decreasing the time to value for AI. Most enterprises won't have in-house rack-scale GPU integration skills, which is why pre-validation and design services are so important.

ASUS says its services run from early facility assessment through to operations. Its professional services cover five offerings: infrastructure design, deployment, performance optimization, AI platform development and lifecycle management. For rapid deployment, ASUS uses its own automation platform, the ASUS Infrastructure Deployment Center (AIDC).

Production needs a partner, not just a part number

So, with an enterprise token factory judged on how reliably it keeps producing rather than on peak FLOPS, in-house AI deployment teams will be back to focusing on the basics, albeit while dealing with an innovative technology. That means they'll be asking questions about sustained performance, heat and power in existing facilities. They'll be looking at integration at the rack level and with management software, along with service windows and deployment time. ASUS is positioning itself as a partner that can answer those questions with the ASUS NVIDIA HGX Rubin System, which it's making available this quarter.

In Bengal, voters await their fate as judicial tribunals’ functioning comes under scrutiny
On September 18, the ECINET portal introduced an OTP-based system to check the status of appeals against exclusion.
Hasana Bibi Molla had voted in four assembly elections when her name was first flagged in January 2026 for logical discrepancy during the West Bengal special intensive revision. Molla, an elector from the Magrahat Paschim assembly constituency, had a spelling mismatch — a common reason for people ending up in the logical discrepancy list, which was 6 million strong at the time. In March, she was cleared by a judicial officer. In the same month, her name was included in the final roll and she voted on April 29 in the assembly elections.
On April 17, she realised her inclusion was challenged by the state’s Chief Electoral Officer (CEO) in front of the judicial tribunal.
Worse, her family says she cannot track the progress of her case on the West Bengal adjudication dashboard on the Election Commission of India’s ECINET portal.
“Whenever we try to log in to the portal, the pop-up says, ‘mobile number not provided while filing the appeal.’ We could track the application before September 18,” Hasana’s nephew, Abdul Halim Molla, told HT.
There was no response from ECI or Bengal CEO.
Also Read: ECI asks states, UTs to rectify electoral rolls during SSR
Hasana has lived in the same locality since 2005 and could link her to the base 2002 SIR list. HT spoke to at least 10 voters across West Bengal who described the same problem. All had been included in the adjudication supplementary lists, and all say the appeals against them became untraceable on the portal after September 18. They are part of the 1.6 million appeals filed by the state CEO against inclusions in the voter list.
Before September 18, electors who had an appeal filed against them could enter their EPIC numbers on the adjudication dashboard on the ECINET portal and it would display their appeal ID and status. For Hasina, the portal showed a ‘pending’ status until September 17 when she last checked.
On September 18, the ECINET portal introduced an OTP-based system to check the status of appeals against exclusion. From then until November 18, the “Track Appeal for Individuals (Under Adjudication)” page on voters.eci.gov.in returned a “Something went wrong” error for voters facing an appeal against their inclusion, according to screen recordings by electors seen by HT.
On Thursday, November 19, the error message changed. When an elector tries to check the status of their appeal, the portal now says: “Mobile number not provided while filing the appeal.”
In an affidavit before the Supreme Court last month, ECI said that of 3.8 million appeals filed before the tribunals, 2.2 million were filed by voters whose names were deleted, and 1.6 million challenged the inclusion of voters. The poll panel told the court that officers of the state CEO’s office filed the 1.6 million appeals against inclusion.
Appeals against inclusion mostly carry 17-digit IDs, while appeals against exclusion carry 20-digit IDs. The 17-digit appeals return the error. The 20-digit ones require an additional OTP, sent to the mobile number the appellant provided during filing. This is separate from the OTP for general account login, as per an analysis by Civic Research Group, a Kolkata-based research collective.
HT reviewed a screen recording of the portal after September 18, in which a known appeal against an elector’s inclusion could not be retrieved. A screenshot from before that date shows the same elector’s appeal, filed on April 5, listed as “pending” and visible to him.
Hasana’s family now has no idea what lies ahead. They have not been summoned to any hearing, and the only local official they could turn to had no answers. “We contacted our BLO who said he has no clue about these appeals. We haven’t received a notice for hearing, yet. Now we can’t even track the appeal status. How will she get back on the roll?” her nephew Abdul asked.
SIR began in West Bengal in November 2025. The draft roll in December removed more than 5.8 million names, which officials attributed to deaths, absence, permanent shifting and duplicate entries.
Also Read: 2.58 crore eligible voters still off UP electoral rolls, says CEO
When the final roll came out on February 28, over 6.3 million, names were deleted, and another 6 million placed “under adjudication”, largely over logical discrepancies in their enumeration forms.
The 19 judicial tribunals’ functioning has come under scrutiny. According to ECI’s affidavit before the top court, only 126,194 appeals were decided by September 21, while 3.7 million were pending. On November 23, the top court asked ECI to set up more tribunals.
For Hasana, until the portal allows access, her family can only wait, with no notice and no way to know how she will stay on the roll.
