Delhi will first open Arvind Kejriwal’s former residence, known as ‘Sheesh Mahal’, to the media before allowing public visits through a ticketing system.
Public Works Department Minister Parvesh Verma announced on Thursday that the Delhi government will open former chief minister Arvind Kejriwal's 'Sheesh Mahal' residence for a media tour initially, and later to the public.
The minister said a ticketing system will be set up for reservation of visits for the public by this week.
"The doors of Sheesh Mahal will open from tomorrow. We will show it to the media," Verma said in a post on X in Hindi, along with a video attached of Kejriwal's first oath-taking ceremony as chief minister of Delhi.
"Looking at public demand, we will open 'Sheesh Mahal' for public tour. We will show the biggest example of corruption to people, that how one person who said he will not even use a government vehicle, had built the lavish residence for himself by demolishing several other houses," the minister had said.
Initially, media tours will be organised; later on, the public can buy tickets and see the interiors of the residence, he added.
According to officials, the ticket price is likely to be around ₹20 and for senior citizens and college students, the entry would be free.
Earlier, the government also announced plans to rope in a private hospitality firm to manage the residence, which would be used for official conferences, lunches and meetings.
"The public viewing will be for a limited period of time; after that, the plan to hand it over to a private hospitality company is in the works; it will be finalised soon," a senior government official said.
The 6, Flagstaff Road bungalow, where former Kejriwal lived during his tenure as chief minister from 2015 to 2024, was nicknamed "Sheesh Mahal" by the BJP to highlight the alleged corruption by the Aam Aadmi Party and its national convener during the Assembly polls held in February 2025.
To maintain these facilities, around 10 staff members are deployed, carrying out sweeping and cleaning of the property. After the Kejriwal family moved out of the controversial residence, PWD carried out an extensive audit of the interiors of the bungalow.

Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are pushing research toward semi-automation: ideas turn into preprints ever faster, and autoresearch pipelines add papers of uneven rigor. When a technique can be overtaken within months, citations arrive too late to tell which new papers deserve reading, so strong work goes unnoticed and newcomers lose their bearings. Yet from the day it appears, a preprint carries the track records of the people and institutions behind it. Established researchers guard their reputations and choose problems and collaborators with research taste, so their involvement tends to raise a paper's quality floor. Building on this signal, we present KnowMe Paper Radar, a lightweight arXiv discovery tool that weights each paper's topical relevance by the reputation its authors and institutions stake on it. Author credit also diffuses by message passing along collaborations to surface rising stars, and institutions are profiled through the researchers they hold in each direction rather than by headcount. In a sealed test on 10,386 new papers, those with an identity-bound author were twice as likely to reach the top tenth of early citations. As its library grows into a scholarly knowledge graph that research agents can query through a command-line interface (CLI), KnowMe also offers a promising literature entry point for future autoresearch and recursive self-improvement (RSI).

articles.title: Tell HN: Lots of Ask HNs again
articles.text:
There have been questions about why the /ask page (https://news.ycombinator.com/ask) was running dry of Ask HNs - e.g.:

Ask HN: Why is Ask HN only showing me 14 posts? - https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49984484 - Oct 2026 (47 comments)

Ask HN: Why is pagination gone on "Ask HN", and showing only 19 items? - https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50280719 - Oct 2026 (3 comments)

I believe I found the problem. The pool of stories for https://news.ycombinator.com/ask has traditionally been drawn from the ranked stories list from which we generate the frontpage. That list is restricted to the top 1500 ranked submissions, and it seems the % of submissions which are text posts (i.e. no linked URL) had declined enough to starve the Ask HN feed. The solution is to compute a separate list of ranked Ask HNs.

p.s. "Ask HN" is the conventional name but it means text posts. The title can also start with "Tell HN" or nothing in particular. They're just posts which were submitted without a URL.
